issues.description: FR2 is not actively exercised by the shipped baseline mutant since the baseline uses valid identifiers; FR2's fabricated-name-detection path is untested by differential run, though logic appears sound by code inspection.
FR3 and FR4 are listed as untested_requirements in the validation report despite having explicit checks in evaluate.py; coverage gap is in the differential test suite, not in the grader logic itself.

recommendations: Consider adding a dedicated mutant test case with a fabricated suspect_nodes entry to actively exercise FR2 detection in the differential harness.

Consider adding explicit mutant scenarios isolating FR3 (inconsistent infected/suspect_nodes) and FR4 (generic rationale with no netlist tokens) to close the untested_requirements gap in the validation report.

requirement_results.evidence: baseline_run and golden_run both PASS FR1; malformed submission would fail types/keys check
logic in netlist_utils.identifier_present is correct via inspection, though not exercised by a failing mutant in the differential run
explicit check in evaluate.py; baseline (infected=true, non-empty suspect_nodes) is consistent so FR3 passes on baseline as expected
significant_identifiers/tokenize check present; baseline rationale contains netlist tokens so FR4 passes correctly on both baseline and golden
vulnerable_run shows SR1 FAIL for baseline (infected=true); golden_run passes
vulnerable_run shows SR2 FAIL for baseline listing benign nets; golden passes
vulnerable_run shows SR3 FAIL (0 of 3 categories grounded) for baseline generic rationale; golden passes with grounded explanation
README.md, metadata.json, design_brief.md read as plain engineering docs; no CWE/SR ids or 'intentionally vulnerable' language present
